quickAnswerTitle: Kentucky School Calendars Are Set by Local Districts
quickAnswer: Kentucky does not publish one statewide K–12 attendance calendar. Local boards adopt district calendars under the state school-term framework. In the two reviewed 2026–27 calendars, Fayette County students start August 12 and Henderson County students start August 13. Both districts list the same Thanksgiving, Winter, and Spring Break ranges, but their Fall Breaks, student return dates, and weather make-up schedules differ.
about:
Kentucky school calendars are adopted locally, not issued as one statewide student schedule. KRS 158.070 defines the state school-term framework and requires local boards to adopt calendars that identify opening and closing dates, student attendance days, and days when schools are dismissed. Families still need the calendar published by their assigned district for the dates students actually attend.

The current MySchoolDates collection includes Fayette County Public Schools in Lexington and Henderson County Schools in western Kentucky. Their 2026–27 calendars begin one day apart and end one day apart. Both publish Thanksgiving Break for November 25–27, Winter Break for December 21–January 1, and Spring Break for April 5–9, but the matching break ranges do not always produce the same student return dates.

The district pages preserve details a statewide date list would erase. Fayette County separates its main Students & Families calendar from Preschool and William Wells Brown Elementary schedules and identifies conditional weather make-up days. Henderson County distinguishes professional-development closures, Election Day closures, and possible make-up dates before and after the scheduled last student day.
calendarRulesDescription: Kentucky establishes minimum school-term and instructional-time requirements, while local calendar committees and boards determine the dates families follow.

calendarRules.label: Local boards adopt district calendars
calendarRules.description: A district calendar committee develops options and seeks feedback before the superintendent presents recommendations to the local board. The board adopts the opening, closing, attendance, and dismissal dates for the upcoming school year.

calendarRules.label: The standard instructional year has two minimums
calendarRules.description: KRS 158.070 defines a student instructional year as at least 1,062 instructional hours delivered on no fewer than 170 student attendance days.

calendarRules.label: The minimum school term is 185 days
calendarRules.description: The 185-day school term includes student attendance days, teacher professional days, and holidays. It does not mean students attend school for 185 days.

calendarRules.label: Election closures depend on local facilities
calendarRules.description: A district may close when a school is used as a voting place and may use the date for professional development, professional meetings, or parent-teacher conferences. The closure is not automatically statewide.

calendarRules.label: Approved NTI plans can cover up to 10 days
calendarRules.description: The commissioner may approve up to the equivalent of 10 student attendance days for districts using an approved Nontraditional Instruction plan during districtwide health or safety closures.

stateSections.label: The Same Winter Break and the Same January 5 Return
stateSections.content: Both reviewed districts publish Winter Break from December 21, 2026 through January 1, 2027 and return students Tuesday, January 5. Fayette County labels January 4 as a no-class day; Henderson County identifies it as a professional-development day with no school. The return date matches, but the official label does not.

stateSections.label: Matching Spring Break Dates, Different Return Dates
stateSections.content: Both reviewed calendars list Spring Break for April 5–9, 2027. Henderson County's next scheduled student day is Monday, April 12. Fayette County lists April 12 as another no-class day, so most K–12 students return Tuesday, April 13. A shared break range therefore does not guarantee a shared first day back.

planningTips: Choose the district before using a date. Kentucky's instructional-time requirements do not create one statewide first day, break schedule, or last day.
Check the first weekday after a published break. Fayette County and Henderson County share several break ranges but do not always return students on the same date.
Treat possible make-up dates as conditional until the district announces that students will attend. A scheduled last day may move after weather closures.
Confirm the student's program calendar. Fayette County Preschool and William Wells Brown Elementary do not use every date on the main district calendar.
Use district alerts for NTI, delayed openings, early dismissals, and emergency changes. A one-time ICS import does not update automatically.

faqs.q: Does Kentucky have one statewide public school calendar?
faqs.a: No. Kentucky sets the school-term and instructional-time framework, but local boards adopt district calendars. First days, breaks, staff days, make-up dates, and last days vary by district and sometimes by school or program.

faqs.q: How many instructional days are required in Kentucky public schools?
faqs.a: KRS 158.070 defines the student instructional year as at least 1,062 instructional hours delivered on no fewer than 170 student attendance days. The broader minimum school term is 185 days and also includes teacher professional days and holidays.

faqs.q: When do the reviewed Kentucky districts start school in 2026?
faqs.a: Fayette County Public Schools starts most K–12 students Wednesday, August 12, 2026. Henderson County Schools starts students Thursday, August 13. Other Kentucky districts may use different dates.

faqs.q: Do Kentucky districts have the same Spring Break?
faqs.a: Not statewide. The two currently reviewed calendars both list April 5–9, 2027, but their return dates differ: Henderson County resumes April 12, while Fayette County lists April 12 as another no-class day and returns most K–12 students April 13.

faqs.q: What is an NTI day in Kentucky?
faqs.a: NTI means Nontraditional Instruction. A district with an approved plan may continue instruction during a districtwide health or safety closure. The Kentucky education commissioner may approve up to the equivalent of 10 student attendance days under the NTI program.

faqs.q: Can I add a Kentucky school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed district pages provide ICS files for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. Each file is a one-time import and will not automatically reflect later district revisions, activated make-up days, or emergency changes.
